REV-1 [R2] Listing a directory touches every child directory just to fill the per-row `locked` flag. The same locked status is already reported when a folder's own level is requested (Listing.locked), so the eager check is extra descendant I/O on every level (worst on slow/network folders and needless work under PERF-001/USR-003). Determine readability lazily when a folder is expanded, or drop the per-entry `locked` flag and rely on the level's own locked reply.

REV-2 [PERF-001] A1's bound relies on 'only row rendering memoised'; that memoisation is defeated by the unstable callback. The cost is bounded by the 1000-row cap but is repeated needless work on low-spec machines. Pass the already-stable editor.openPath directly or a useCallback-wrapped handler from App so unchanged rows are skipped.

REV-3 [USR-006] The reset is meant to discard temporary Up navigation and follow the automatic root; clearing expansion is not required when the root is unchanged. As written, the R3 browse-and-open flow forces the user to re-expand the same folders after every file they open (extra effort the R2 explorer is meant to remove). Only reset expansion when the automatic root actually changes, or preserve the expanded set across active-tab changes within one root.

QA-1 [R3] R3 acceptance 'Clicking an image or other binary-preview file opens the editor's existing preview form' has no test at all. Add a test that lists an image/PDF in the explorer, clicks it, and asserts the editor's preview form is shown (e.g. 'Preview of ...' or the preview test id) rather than a text editor.

QA-2 [R4] R4 acceptance 'Switching the active tab between files owned by different apps moves the root to the newly active tab's owning app' is only proven compositionally, not by a test that performs that switch.
QA-3 [R4] R4 acceptance 'Changing the root does not close or alter any open tab' is asserted only as a tab count, not that each open tab (and its content) is unchanged.
QA-4 [R2] Add a test that opens a file from the explorer, then collapses its folder, and asserts the editor tab remains open.

QA-5 [R2] R2 edge case 'A folder with thousands of entries shows a loading indication and keeps the window responsive while it loads' is only partially covered (loading shown, no scale/responsiveness check). EFF-002 is relaxed, so this is advisory.
QA-6 [R3] R3 edge case 'Clicking a file does not modify its contents on disk' has no test asserting the click only reads.
QA-7 [R3] R3 edge case 'Opening a file does not close or change other open tabs' is not asserted after an explorer click.
QA-8 [R1] R1 edge case 'a file that is already open is focused instead of duplicated' is not exercised through the palette picker path.
QA-9 [R1] R1's 'in every view' is not tested for the editor view.

SEC-1 [USR-003] 'Show hidden' and refresh fire one full directory scan per currently expanded folder simultaneously. Each request is bounded (1000 returned / 10000 scanned) and lazy, and the trigger is user-initiated, so this is not a remote or unbounded-input DoS; but a burst of blocking-pool scans over a slow disk or network folder can stall the window on low-spec hardware. Worth a concurrency cap or sequential refresh in a later pass.
